title: Cabinet Clears Delimitation Bill With 50% Seat Rise for Every State, Freeze Till 2051
excerpt: The Union Cabinet on Friday cleared a fresh Constitution Amendment Bill linking women's reservation to delimitation, with a uniform 50% increase in Lok Sabha seats for every state and the existing inter-state ratio sealed until 2051. The bill goes before a special sitting of Parliament beginning November 30.
body:
• The Union Cabinet on Friday, November 27, cleared a fresh Constitution Amendment Bill that links women's reservation to delimitation and raises every state's Lok Sabha seats by a uniform 50%.
  • The existing inter-state share of seats, based on the 1971 population, would be sealed until 2051, and the increased seats would be redrawn using the 2011 Census, sources said.
  • The Lok Sabha's maximum strength would rise from the present 543 seats to 850; a constitutional amendment needs a two-thirds majority in both Houses.
  • Parliament sits specially from November 30: the Lok Sabha on November 30 and December 1; the Rajya Sabha on December 2 and 3. The opposition INDIA bloc meets on Saturday to decide its strategy.

The Union Cabinet, chaired by Prime Minister Narendra Modi, on Friday, cleared a fresh Constitution Amendment Bill to implement reservation for women in Parliament and state legislatures through a delimitation exercise. The revised bill answers the objection that sank the government's earlier attempt in April: this time, Lok Sabha seats would rise by 50 per cent in every state, so no state loses relative ground to another.

How the formula works

Delimitation is the redrawing of constituency boundaries and the allocation of seats between states. Its political difficulty is well known: states that controlled population growth fear losing parliamentary share to states that did not. The fresh bill addresses that directly. According to sources cited by BusinessLine, the Cabinet approved amendments ensuring that no state loses its representation in the Lok Sabha in proportion to other states after delimitation. Every state's seats rise by the same 50 per cent, the current inter-state ratio of parliamentary constituencies in both Houses — based on the 1971 population — is sealed till 2051, and the increased seats are to be redrawn using the 2011 Census.

The proposed amendment would increase the strength of the Lok Sabha from the present 543 seats to a maximum of 850 through delimitation. The treasury benches said the move will pave the way for implementing 33 per cent reservation for women in Parliament and state legislative assemblies ahead of the 2029 general election. The Cabinet meeting was convened at 1 pm at Sewa Teerth, the Prime Minister's Office complex.

What changed from the failed April bill

The earlier version of the bill was introduced during a special sitting in April and fell short of the required two-thirds majority in the Lok Sabha. It did not include the provision to increase seats across all states by 50 per cent; that uniform increase is the new element in the revised bill, aimed at addressing southern states' concerns. The government has now claimed it has the numbers to pass the legislation. YourStory reported that the DMK and NCP, besides the BRS, are expected to support the bill. Those expectations are the government's, and the opposition INDIA bloc — which is against the legislation — will meet on Saturday to discuss its strategy.

What happens next

On Thursday, the government asked the presiding officers of both Houses to reconvene Parliament to transact essential government business. A four-day special sitting has been called: November 30 and December 1 in the Lok Sabha, and December 2 and 3 in the Rajya Sabha. A two-thirds majority in both Houses is required for a constitutional amendment bill to pass.

"When the government calls a session or a special session, that means there are very important bills or business for the nation."

— Kiren Rijiju, Parliamentary Affairs Minister

For readers, nothing changes yet: constituency boundaries, seat counts, and women's reservation all remain as they are unless and until the amendment passes both Houses in the coming sitting and completes the remaining constitutional steps. The first test is the Lok Sabha vote on November 30 and December 1.
nri_angle: The bill would reshape Lok Sabha representation and activate 33% women's reservation; diaspora readers with family constituencies in India will see boundaries and seat counts change only if the amendment clears both Houses in the November 30 sitting.
